skill_title: Predict molecular shape (VSEPR) and bond polarity

items.question: What does VSEPR theory predict?
items.expectedAnswer: The shape of a molecule, from the repulsion of electron pairs around the central atom.
items.explanation: VSEPR (Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion) predicts molecular shape from electron-pair repulsion.
options: The shape of a molecule, from the repulsion of electron pairs around the central atom.

items.question: According to VSEPR, electron pairs around a central atom arrange themselves to be...
items.explanation: Electron pairs repel and spread out to minimise repulsion (maximum separation).

items.question: A molecule with two bonding pairs and no lone pairs on the central atom is...
items.explanation: Two pairs spread to opposite sides, giving a linear shape (e.g. CO₂, BeCl₂).

items.question: A molecule with four bonding pairs and no lone pairs (like CH₄) is...
items.explanation: Four bonding pairs spread out into a tetrahedral shape (e.g. methane).

items.question: What is electronegativity?
items.expectedAnswer: An atom's ability to attract the shared electrons in a bond.
items.explanation: Electronegativity measures how strongly an atom pulls bonding electrons.
options: The energy needed to remove an electron.
An atom's ability to attract the shared electrons in a bond.
The number of electrons in an atom.

items.question: A bond between two identical atoms (e.g. Cl₂) is...
items.explanation: Identical atoms have equal electronegativity, so the bond is non-polar.

items.question: A large difference in electronegativity between two bonded atoms gives a bond that is...
items.explanation: A big electronegativity difference means electrons are largely transferred — an ionic/strongly polar bond.

items.question: A water molecule (H₂O) has 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs on oxygen. Its shape is...
items.explanation: Two lone pairs push the bonds together, giving water a bent shape.

items.question: Ammonia (NH₃) has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair on nitrogen. Its shape is...
items.explanation: The lone pair makes ammonia trigonal pyramidal (not flat trigonal planar).

items.question: Why must lone pairs be counted when predicting shape?
items.expectedAnswer: Lone pairs also repel and change the angles and shape.
items.explanation: Lone pairs occupy space and repel bonding pairs, altering the molecular shape.
options: Lone pairs also repel and change the angles and shape.

items.question: A molecule with three bonding pairs and no lone pairs (like BF₃) has the shape...
items.explanation: Three bonding pairs and no lone pairs give a flat trigonal planar shape.

items.question: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) has polar C=O bonds but is a NON-polar molecule. Why?
items.expectedAnswer: Its linear, symmetrical shape makes the bond polarities cancel.
items.explanation: The two equal, opposite bond dipoles cancel in the linear molecule, so CO₂ is non-polar overall.
options: Its linear, symmetrical shape makes the bond polarities cancel.

items.question: Why is water (H₂O) a polar molecule even though it has the same type of bonds as CO₂?
items.expectedAnswer: Its bent shape means the bond dipoles do not cancel.
items.explanation: Water's bent shape leaves a net dipole (the bond polarities do not cancel), making it polar.
options: Its bent shape means the bond dipoles do not cancel.

items.question: Which molecule is non-polar overall?
items.explanation: CH₄'s symmetrical tetrahedral shape cancels the bond dipoles, so it is non-polar.

items.question: In a polar covalent bond, the more electronegative atom carries a...
items.explanation: The more electronegative atom pulls the shared electrons closer, gaining a partial negative charge (δ−).

items.question: Which factor decides whether a molecule with polar bonds is polar overall?
items.expectedAnswer: Its shape (symmetry) — symmetrical molecules can be non-polar.
items.explanation: Molecular shape determines whether bond dipoles cancel (non-polar) or add (polar).
options: Its shape (symmetry) — symmetrical molecules can be non-polar.

items.question: A central atom is surrounded by 4 electron pairs, of which 1 is a lone pair. The molecular shape is...
items.explanation: 4 pairs with 1 lone pair gives trigonal pyramidal (like NH₃).

items.question: Which bond is the most polar?
items.explanation: H–F has the largest electronegativity difference of these, so it is the most polar.

items.question: Why does a lone pair push bonding pairs closer together than another bonding pair would?
items.expectedAnswer: A lone pair repels more strongly than a bonding pair.
items.explanation: Lone pairs exert greater repulsion, compressing the bond angles (e.g. H₂O's angle < 109.5°).
options: A lone pair repels more strongly than a bonding pair.
A lone pair has no charge.
A lone pair attracts the bonds.

items.question: A molecule is symmetrical and all its outer atoms are identical. Even with polar bonds, it is likely...
items.explanation: Symmetry with identical outer atoms causes bond dipoles to cancel, giving a non-polar molecule.
